I recommend deliver because both problems can be repaired inside this PR and it is your own.

After keeps all of that, so the functionality-only wording is delivered, but this case does not show a gain. The weakest point in After is standing in snapshot A: the second part now opens with only "Two problems block merging:", and the still-running required unit check has moved two paragraphs down, after the comment sentence, where it no longer reads as something that must finish before merge. I counted it as holding because the check is still called required and still running, but it is borderline; restore Before's shape, e.g. "Two problems block merging, and a required unit check is still running in CI." After's sync sentence is slightly better than Before's, since it drops the unsupplied "and pushed" and keeps "no commits were dropped". Its C report states the block twice ("GitHub reports the merge as blocked for you" and "Merge is not offered because GitHub blocks this actor"); one sentence is enough, but keep it in prose so it never becomes a "Not offered:" line.
